title: Leon Doucette becomes Cape Ann Museum's Curator of the Collections
summary: The Cape Ann Museum announced the promotion of Assistant Curator Leon Doucette to Curator of the Collections. A Gloucester native and acclaimed artist, Doucette has been a key member of CAM’s Curatorial Department since 2011, working alongside Henrietta Gates & Heaton Robertson Chief Curator Martha Oaks. In his new role, Doucette will oversee the management, interpretation, and ongoing development of the Museum’s permanent collection. “Leon Doucette is an invaluable colleague and an extraordinary steward of Cape Ann’s stories,” said Museum Director Oliver Barker. “His deep knowledge of the Museum’s vast and growing collections—from paintings, photographs, textiles, drawings, and sculpture to maritime history and other significant artifacts—gives him a rare ability to see the connections among the people, places, objects, and stories

title: Everard's Oct. 27-29 auction offers a rich array of fine & decorative art, antiques, and luxury goods
summary: Everard’s October 27-29 live online auction offers collectors and interior-design connoisseurs a breathtaking selection of fine and decorative art from Southern estates, distinguished residences and long-held collections. While the timeline represented traverses nearly three centuries of important art movements and flourishing cultures, the fall event’s abundant variety is bound by a single common theme: uncompromising quality. Its 1,470 expertly-curated lots represent the ultimate in modern and contemporary fine art, antique and mid-century modern furniture, automobilia and advertising, vintage concert posters, Inuit and Native American art, Savannah and Southern artworks, books and manuscripts, and Asian art. The entire third session on October 29 is devoted to elegant jewelry and luxury goods from top-tier brands and designers, including Tiffany, Cartier, Dior, Chanel, Gucci and more. title: Fred Holabird to come out of retirement on November 6 to auction over 200 lots
summary: Reports of Fred Holabird’s professional retirement have been greatly exaggerated. The veteran auctioneer and owner of Holabird Western Americana Collections, LLC has been in a self-imposed retirement since his Grand Finale auction last year. But he’s saddling up again, this time to auction The Jack Haddock Nevada Town Token Collection on Friday, November 6. The live auction is being hosted exclusively on iCollector.com, starting at 8am Pacific Time. It’s packed with 250 lots of vintage and antique Nevada tokens, most of them metal but some paper and celluloid plastic. Half of the tokens up for bid are either unique or one of just a few known. Most of the businesses issuing tokens were saloons, hence the 12 ½ cent value or “one bit” drink. title: In Memoriam: Renowned anthropologist and Pre-Columbian scholar Bob Pickering
summary: Bob Pickering was an anthropologist, archaeologist, forensic anthropologist, museum curator and educator whose career ranged from identifying the remains of American servicemen to investigating the authenticity of ancient West Mexican ceramics. I first knew Bob when he was at the Children’s Museum of Indianapolis and I was visiting the city. Looking back over his career, what strikes me is how consistently he approached objects as evidence. Art was something to look at, certainly, but it was also something to question, investigate and use to understand the people who made it. Pickering trained in physical anthropology and received his Ph.D. from Northwestern University in 1984. In 1975–76, he worked at the U.S. Army identification laboratory in Thailand, helping identify the remains of American servicemen from the Vietnam War. title: Peter Wächtler explores language, nostalgia, and cinematic illusion at Haus am Waldsee
summary: Peter Wächtler’s forthcoming exhibition Ständig at Haus am Waldsee brings together new and existing works, most notably a new eponymous film. Through classic animation and elaborate set construction with extreme angles and distorted perspectives, the film draws on techniques from theatre and early cinema. Based on a poem by the artist, it stages formulaic movements and speech across four chapters, arranged around the inherent logics of the German conjunctions “und,” “oder,” “aber,” and “denn” (and, or, but, because). Wächtler’s elaborate practice goes beyond fixed classifications. title: Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw presents major contemporary survey 'Sculpture Beyond the Solid'
summary: The medium of sculpture is quick to react to the ever-changing reality—and the new show at MSN takes a broad and closer look at those reactions. More than fifty works by international artists are going on display in all parts of the Museum, from the outdoor walkways to the second-floor galleries; some are being specially produced for the occasion. The exhibition Sculpture Beyond the Solid opens on October 16. A towering piece, almost three meters high, in patinated bronze. This is Alina Szapocznikow’s Friendship (Monument to Polish-Soviet Friendship), greeting visitors on the first floor at MSN since the new site of the Museum opened two years ago. A representation of two men, larger than life. Back in 1954, it was intended as a symbol—for years ahead, for decades to follow, for ages; today, it tells a different story: about the eventual fall of the colossus, about weakness and fragility hidden behind the façade, about radical change. title: Pre-Hispanic solar observatory discovered at Teteles de Ávila Castillo in Puebla
summary: Archaeologists working at Teteles de Ávila Castillo in the Sierra Norte of Puebla have confirmed that a monumental architectural complex at the site functioned as a solar observatory more than 2,500 years ago, a discovery that could reshape understanding of astronomical knowledge and cultural connections in ancient Mesoamerica. Research conducted by Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH) indicates that the complex, known as Group E or Tetelihtic, was deliberately laid out according to observations of the sun, surrounding mountains and broader astronomical horizon. According to the archaeological team, the site may represent the oldest known complex of its kind in Mexico and the first documented outside the Maya region. title: Derek Eller Gallery presents EJ Hauser's solo exhibition 'Sun Water Sky'
summary: Derek Eller Gallery is presenting a solo show of new work by EJ Hauser entitled Sun Water Sky. Inspired by natural phenomena, guided by a process that begins with drawing, and mindful of the act of observation, Hauser makes paintings which fluidly exist between abstraction and representation, combining the graphic symbolism of repeated motifs with the gestural language of poetry. Mostly intimate in scale, the paintings in this exhibition invite close viewing, an immersive concentration which effectively “opens the imagination to something vast” according to Hauser. This act of beholding is central to the work. For Stars Reflected, Hauser recalls the magical experience of falling asleep in the studio and waking up in the night to the sight of the calm creek outside their window, perfectly reflecting the celestial sky. title: Pace Gallery anchors Art Basel Paris 2026 booth with Jean Dubuffet and multigenerational lineup
summary: Pace’s presentation (#A30) at Art Basel Paris 2026 will spotlight a multigenerational group of artists, encompassing historic works as well as paintings, sculptures, and works on paper by contemporary practitioners. The gallery’s booth will be anchored by a selection of paintings by Jean Dubuffet, celebrating Pace’s longstanding relationship with the pioneering French artist. Pace has represented Dubuffet for nearly 60 years, with the artist joining the gallery in 1967 and presenting his first solo show, Painted Sculptures, in New York in 1968. The paintings on view at Art Basel reflect Dubuffet’s bold departures from art historical traditions and his lasting impact on contemporary art. This impact can be felt in the progressive practices of present-day artists showing on Pace’s booth, including Yto Barrada, Lynda Benglis, Nigel Cooke, Mary Corse, Elmgreen & Dragset, Pam Evelyn, Huong Dodinh, Loie Hollowell, Alicja Kwade, Li Songsong, Lee Ufan,

title: Christie's London 20/21 Evening Sales total £219 million │ +103 % YoY
summary: On 14 October 2026, Christie's London combined 20/21 Evening Sales generated a total of £218,603,400 /$289,430,902 /€258,389,219, with a 103% increase on the total achieved last year. Our running total for 20/21 sales year to date sits at £494 million with five sales to come in the Marquee Week. Tonight's auctions realised sell-through rates of 91% by lot and 96% by value. In an auction rich with extraordinary international works, two museum-quality masterpieces – Wassily Kandinsky's Das bunte Leben (1907) and Piet Mondrian's Composition III (1920) - achieved over £25 million each. More than 10,000 people visited the Christie's galleries during the exhibition at King Street, drawn by the exceptional pieces exhibited. title: Johnny Miller explores inequality and transformed landscapes at Amerikahaus Munich
summary: Amerikahaus Munich is presenting two major bodies of work by American photographer Johnny Miller in Unequal Scenes & Salt Works, an exhibition that examines how social inequality, industrial activity and human intervention become visible when landscapes are viewed from above. On view from October 16, 2026 through January 9, 2027, the exhibition brings together Miller's internationally recognized Unequal Scenes project with his more recent explorations of industrial salt landscapes. Presented in collaboration with Buchkunst Berlin, the show highlights the photographer's ability to move between documentary observation and near-abstraction while addressing some of the defining social and environmental questions of the present. title: Museum Folkwang pairs Herbert W. Franke and Gottfried Jäger in dialogue on early digital art
summary: From 16 October 2026 to 10 January 2027, the Museum Folkwang will be hosting the exhibition Herbert W. Franke / Gottfried Jäger. Art and Construction. The exhibition marks a major donation to the Museum Folkwang of photographs, prints, videos and computer animations from Herbert W. Franke’s body of work. For the first time, around 250 works by the two artists will be presented together in a dialogic format. The focus is on their artistic exchange between non-representational photography and early computer art, which began in the 1960s. The starting point for this dialogue is the book Art and Construction by the computer pioneer, caver and science fiction author Herbert W. title: Alexander Tutsek-Stiftung presents major 20-year retrospective of the C/O Berlin Talent Award
summary: Starting on 16 October 2026, the Alexander Tutsek-Stiftung will present the large-scale exhibition "Photography in Flux. 20 Years C/O Berlin Talent Award" on both exhibition levels of the BlackBox and the BlackBox FirstFloor in Munich’s Parkstadt Schwabing. C/O Berlin is one of Europe’s most renowned exhibition venues for photography and lens-based media. In addition to its highly acclaimed exhibition program, C/O Berlin annually presents the C/O Berlin Talent Award. In a way that remains unique to this day, the prize honors a tandem of an Artist and a Writer, thereby fostering a dialogue between photography as a practice and as an academic discipline. title: ARKO Art Center unveils major collection survey highlighting 50 years of Korean contemporary art
summary: The history of the ARKO Art Center collection and its acquisition process is closely connected to the Korean Culture and Arts Foundation (now Arts Council Korea, or ARKO), an organization established in 1973 to implement the Korean government’s culture and arts promotion policies, and to the exhibition history of the Misulhoegwan (now ARKO Art Center), which has been operated by the council. When the Misulhoegwan first opened in 1974, during a period when Korea was lacking in cultural infrastructure, it offered exhibition space for rent at a relatively low cost, supporting the activities of experimental young and emerging artists as well as various groups. title: Palm Springs Art Museum presents first comprehensive survey of Lita Albuquerque
summary: Palm Springs Art Museum announces Lita Albuquerque: Cosmic Land, a solo exhibition on view October 16, 2026 through May 3, 2027. Spanning nearly six decades of her practice, the exhibition marks the first time the celebrated California artist's paintings, sculptures, installations, and films are brought together in a single exhibition. Guiding viewers through a continuous, unfolding journey, Cosmic Land traces the relationship between Earth and cosmos, revealing the terrestrial and celestial as inseparable and the human being as belonging to both at once. title: IFA art collection exhibition 'Action Bodies' explores movement, collective action, and space
summary: The exhibition Action Bodies continues the artistic-curatorial exploration of the ifa art collection with a focus on how spaces and bodies are perceived and shaped through movement and collective action. Selected artworks from the ifa collection are presented alongside contemporary perspectives, illuminating social orders and opening up possibilities for resistance. In this space of co-existence, textile objects, hybrid bodies and social choreographies gradually unfold. Franz Erhard Walther has been creating interactive textile sculptures since the early 1960s, declaring action an art form in itself and turning viewers into key actors. An important source of inspiration for this exhibition is his “action bodies”, which intertwine object and process, individuals and groups, elements of separation and connection. title: Crespo Foundation presents 'Aftergrowth' featuring Glenkeen Garden artists in Frankfurt
summary: “Gardening is a commitment to the future, blind like any act of faith.” Derek Jarman. Glenkeen Garden—“beautiful valley” in Irish—grew out of a similar commitment. For over twenty years, photographer and Crespo Foundation founder Ulrike Crespo (1950 – 2019) worked a stretch of waterlogged farmland overlooking Roaringwater Bay on Ireland's southwest coast into a vast landscaped garden; half cultivated, half kept wild. Her wish was for it to remain, after her passing, a place of contemplation, creative experimentation, and communing. Since 2021, Glenkeen Garden Residencies has brought together artists, writers, musicians, and thinkers who, immerse themselves in the garden and, in a way, continue its caretaking. title: Istituto Svizzero in Rome opens annual group exhibition 'Outlaws'
summary: The annual group exhibition of the Istituto Svizzero in Rome is titled Outlaws. The project takes the concept of law as its point of departure, questioning its nature as a human convention that appears immutable yet is often subject to historical shifts and internal tensions. The works examine what – and whom – the law governs, and who instead positions themselves above or outside it. These questions unfold across different historical periods and stories, often set in Switzerland. They also engage with the poetic, formal, and sometimes humorous dimensions of legal structures, exploring how rules and diplomacy can shape social realities and open new imaginative possibilities for understanding social justice and human coexistence. title: Tokyo Arts and Space marks 20-year Seoul exchange with commemorative TOKAS Project exhibition
summary: The TOKAS Project is designed to foster international exchange and inspire reflection on diverse themes such as art and society from multicultural perspectives. In commemoration of the 20th anniversary of the exchange between Tokyo Arts and Space (TOKAS) and the partner institutions of Seoul, South Korea, the project welcomes five artists from Japan and South Korea, Eun Jae Pil, Kim Dohee, Koo Donghee, Mino Arata, Park Minha, who have previously participated in the residency program, and who reimagine reality through their own bodily experiences. Throughout the history of art, people have sought to remove the world before them and the living beings around them from the flow of time, anchoring them in place through painting, sculpture, photography, film, and the moving image, in an attempt to imbue them with immortality. title: MCA Australia presents major posthumous retrospective of pioneering Māori artist Robyn Kahukiwa
summary: The Museum of Contemporary Art Australia (MCA Australia) presents My Ancestors Are Always With Me, a major exhibition celebrating the life, work and enduring legacy of Māori artist Robyn Kahukiwa (1938–2025). Developed in partnership with Christchurch Art Gallery Te Puna o Waiwhetū, the exhibition is the first Australian solo exhibition dedicated to the Sydney-born artist, bringing together works spanning more than five decades. Opening at MCA Australia in the wake of Kahukiwa's passing, the exhibition offers audiences a timely opportunity to encounter the extraordinary vision of an artist whose work transformed representations of Māori identity, culture and political struggle. title: LABoral Centro de Arte y Creación Industrial presents video art installation by Analivia Cordeiro
summary: LABoral Centro de Arte y Creacion Industrial launches its new Guest Artwork programme with a video installation coming from the NEWART foundation: Cambiantes (1976/2015), by Brazilian artist and dancer Analivia Cordeiro. Considered a seminal work in the history of video art and video dance, Cambiantes will be exhibited at LABoral from October 2 until March 27. A pioneering work of video art in Brazil and one of the earliest international experiments in video dance, the piece explores the relationships between the body, movement, image and technology. The three-channel video installation created in 2015 draws on the audiovisual material of the original Cambiantes video (1976), while incorporating a new edit and revisiting the spatial concept of the original work: a human-scale cube. title: Luis Royo fantasy masterpiece leads Heritage's Oct. 24-25 International Comic Art Auction
summary: Collectors who aspire to own one of the most influential and recognizable images in contemporary fantasy art have the opportunity to make that dream come true at Heritage Auctions’ International Comic Art Signature® Auction Oct. 24–25 when Luis Royo’s Los Hilos de los Sueños crosses the block during the Platinum Session.
